Executive Director of the Emory Empathetic AI for Health Institute and Robert W. Woodruff Professor of Biomedical Engineering, Emory University, United States of America
Dr. Anant Madabhushi is the Robert W Woodruff Professor of Biomedical Engineering; and on the faculty in the Departments of Pathology, Biomedical Informatics, Urology and Radiology and Imaging Sciences at Emory University. He is a researcher within the Cancer Immunology program at the Winship Cancer Center and also a Research Career Scientist at the Atlanta Veterans Administration Medical Center. Dr. Madabhushi has authored over 500 peer-reviewed publications and more than 200 patents issued or pending.
He is a Fellow of the American Institute of Medical and Biological Engineering (AIMBE), Fellow of the Institute for Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE), Fellow of the American Association for Advancement of Science (AAAS) and a Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors (NAI). His work on "Smart Imaging Computers for Identifying lung cancer patients who need chemotherapy" was called out by Prevention Magazine as one of the top 10 medical breakthroughs of 2018. In 2019, Nature Magazine hailed him as one of 5 scientists developing "offbeat and innovative approaches for cancer research". Dr. Madabhushi was named to The Pathologist’s Power List in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022.

people.bio:
Minister of Intellectual Property, Republic of Korea
H.E. Dr. KIM Yong Sun is Minister of Intellectual Property of the Republic of Korea. He has extensive experience in intellectual property policy, administration and international cooperation, having held a range of senior leadership positions within the Korean intellectual property system.
Prior to his appointment as Minister in November 2025, he served as President of the Korea Intellectual Property Protection Agency (KOIPA) and Vice Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO). His previous roles at KIPO include Director-General of the Industrial Property Policy Bureau, Chief Presiding Administrative Judge of the IP Trial and Appeal Board (IPTAB), and Director of the Intellectual Property Policy Division. Dr. Kim holds a J.S.D. and LL.M. in Intellectual Property Law from Washington University in St. Louis School of Law and a B.A. of Urban Administration from the University of Seoul.

people.bio:
Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs, Singapore

As Minister for Law, Mr. Tong leads efforts to uphold the rule of law, strengthen Singapore’s legal framework, and advance access to justice. He also advances Singapore’s position as an international hub for legal services, dispute resolution, intellectual property, and restructuring and insolvency. Minister of Science and Culture, Finland
Born on 11 June 1980 in Vaasa, Mari-Leena Talvitie (nee Kairivaara) grew up in a family of entrepreneurs in South Ostrobothnia. Having completed her matriculation examination at the general upper secondary school of Ilmajoki in 1999, she then studied at the University of Oulu and graduated as a Master of Science in environmental technology in 2010.
Talvitie first became a Member of Parliament from the electoral district of Oulu in 2015. Since then, she has served as Vice-Chair of the Administration Committee and been a member of various parliamentary committees, such as the Education and Culture Committee, the Environment Committee and the Legal Affairs Committee. Talvitie has been a Member of the Finnish Delegation to the Arctic Parliamentary Conference throughout her years as a Member of Parliament. She has also served as vice-chair of the National Coalition Party's parliamentary group.
Over the course of her political career, she has held the position of vice-chair of the National Coalition Party and chair of the party council of the National Coalition Party. Talvitie has been a member of the Oulu City Council since 2005. She has also chaired the Oulu City Executive, Oulu City Council, Oulu Regional Environmental Committee, Educational Consortium OSAO, and North Ostrobothnia Regional Assembly. people.bio:
Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer,
Sakana AI, Japan

Ren co-founded Sakana AI in 2023, a Tokyo-based AI company creating a new kind of foundational AI models based on nature-inspired intelligence. Sakana AI has become Japan’s fastest unicorn after one year in business, backed by Nvidia and a broad spectrum of Japanese enterprises including the 3 Japanese Megabanks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) and other leading companies in each of Japan’s industry sectors. In 2025, Sakana AI became the largest unicorn Japan has ever had.

Prior to Sakana, Ren took the lead on the global expansion of Mercari, Japan’s first unicorn start-up running the fastest-growing marketplace app. He served as CEO of Mercari Europe, as well as successfully orchestrated its IPO valuing the company at $6bn.

Before tech, Ren spent 15 years as a Japanese diplomat where he worked on the security alliance with the US, negotiated a free trade agreement with the EU, and represented Japan at the World Bank board. Ren continues to be involved in public policy debates on technological innovation and international politics as Senior Fellow at New York University (NYU) School of Law, and is the youngest member of the Trilateral Commission.

Ren received his Master of Laws from NYU School of Law (2004) and Bachelor of Laws from the University of Tokyo (2001) and is admitted to practice law in New York. Ren also holds a Master of Arts in East Asian Studies from Stanford University (2005).

Head of the IP Practice, Allen & Gledhill LLP, Singapore
Dr Stanley Lai is a Senior Counsel who specialises in all forms of IP litigation/arbitration and information technology disputes and is also a commercial litigator and SIAC Arbitrator. Over 27 years of legal practice he has argued many significant cases before the Singapore Courts as well as the Singapore International Commercial Court, spanning a range of different subject areas. He also maintains a strong practice for IP/data management and cybersecurity, serving a broad spectrum of clients. In the sphere of artificial intelligence, Stanley continues to advise clients on issues relating to intellectual property, data protection, content regulation as well as legal tech. Stanley currently serves as the Deputy President of the Copyright Tribunal and sits on the panel of Arbitrators in the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, specializing in the intellectual property disputes. From 1 July 2026, Stanley has been appointed Chairperson of the Data Protection Appeal (DPAP), an independent body that hears appeals against directions or decisions of the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) in relation to data protection provisions in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). From 2026, Stanley has also been appointed to serve as a neutral in the newly formed Patent Mediation and Arbitration Centre under the Unified Patent Court (Europe). Stanley also serves as a Senior Mediator of the Singapore Mediation Centre and as a Specialist Mediator of the Singapore International Mediation Centre. He is an author of many published journal articles and was the first Singapore born lawyer to be conferred a PhD by the University of Cambridge (UK). Stanley was formerly the Chairman of the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS). He was awarded the Public Service Medal (Pingat Bakit Masyarakat) in 2020, and the Public Service Star (Bintang Bakti Masyarakat) in 2024. On 31 August 2022, Stanley was awarded the Singapore Academy of Law Merit Award, which is an award given to individuals who have served in promoting and advancing the objectives of the Singapore Academy of Law. Stanley was appointed Senior Counsel in 2010.

Gaétan de Rassenfosse is an Associate Professor of Science, Technology and Innovation Policy at the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland. Trained as an economist, he studies how intellectual property and innovation policies shape the creation, diffusion, and commercialization of knowledge. He holds a Ph.D. in Economics from the Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium.
His research bridges economics, management, and law. His publications have appeared in a wide range of journals, including the Journal of Industrial Economics, Strategic Management Journal, Research Policy, Journal of Law and Economics, Southern California Law Review, among others. His most recent work addresses patent quality, knowledge disclosure, technology commercialization, and the implications of AI-generated inventions for the patent system. He combines economic analysis with large-scale data to examine how intellectual property institutions serve innovators and society.
At EPFL, he teaches intellectual property management and the economics of innovation, introducing students from different disciplines to the economic foundations, legal principles, and strategic uses of IP. He writes The Patentist, a publication that makes economic research on patents accessible to policymakers, practitioners, and a wider audience.
Across his research, teaching, and public engagement, he seeks to bring empirical evidence to debates about how intellectual property can support innovation and the public interest.

Associate Professor of Science Technology and Innovation Policy, Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, Belgium
Gaétan de Rassenfosse is an Associate Professor of Science, Technology and Innovation Policy at the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland. Trained as an economist, he studies how intellectual property and innovation policies shape the creation, diffusion, and commercialization of knowledge. He holds a Ph.D. in Economics from the Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium.
His research bridges economics, management, and law. His publications have appeared in a wide range of journals, including the Journal of Industrial Economics, Strategic Management Journal, Research Policy, Journal of Law and Economics, Southern California Law Review, among others. His most recent work addresses patent quality, knowledge disclosure, technology commercialization, and the implications of AI-generated inventions for the patent system. He combines economic analysis with large-scale data to examine how intellectual property institutions serve innovators and society.
At EPFL, he teaches intellectual property management and the economics of innovation, introducing students from different disciplines to the economic foundations, legal principles, and strategic uses of IP. He writes The Patentist, a publication that makes economic research on patents accessible to policymakers, practitioners, and a wider audience.
Across his research, teaching, and public engagement, he seeks to bring empirical evidence to debates about how intellectual property can support innovation and the public interest.

people.bio:
Head of the IP Practice, Allen & Gledhill LLP, Singapore
Dr Stanley Lai is a Senior Counsel who specialises in all forms of IP litigation/arbitration and information technology disputes and is also a commercial litigator and SIAC Arbitrator. Over 27 years of legal practice he has argued many significant cases before the Singapore Courts as well as the Singapore International Commercial Court, spanning a range of different subject areas. He also maintains a strong practice for IP/data management and cybersecurity, serving a broad spectrum of clients. In the sphere of artificial intelligence, Stanley continues to advise clients on issues relating to intellectual property, data protection, content regulation as well as legal tech. Stanley currently serves as the Deputy President of the Copyright Tribunal and sits on the panel of Arbitrators in the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, specializing in the intellectual property disputes. From 1 July 2026, Stanley has been appointed Chairperson of the Data Protection Appeal (DPAP), an independent body that hears appeals against directions or decisions of the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) in relation to data protection provisions in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). From 2026, Stanley has also been appointed to serve as a neutral in the newly formed Patent Mediation and Arbitration Centre under the Unified Patent Court (Europe). Stanley also serves as a Senior Mediator of the Singapore Mediation Centre and as a Specialist Mediator of the Singapore International Mediation Centre. He is an author of many published journal articles and was the first Singapore born lawyer to be conferred a PhD by the University of Cambridge (UK). Stanley was formerly the Chairman of the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS). He was awarded the Public Service Medal (Pingat Bakit Masyarakat) in 2020, and the Public Service Star (Bintang Bakti Masyarakat) in 2024. On 31 August 2022, Stanley was awarded the Singapore Academy of Law Merit Award, which is an award given to individuals who have served in promoting and advancing the objectives of the Singapore Academy of Law. Stanley was appointed Senior Counsel in 2010.

Head of the IP Practice, Allen & Gledhill LLP, Singapore
Dr Stanley Lai is a Senior Counsel who specialises in all forms of IP litigation/arbitration and information technology disputes and is also a commercial litigator and SIAC Arbitrator. Over 27 years of legal practice he has argued many significant cases before the Singapore Courts as well as the Singapore International Commercial Court, spanning a range of different subject areas. He also maintains a strong practice for IP/data management and cybersecurity, serving a broad spectrum of clients. In the sphere of artificial intelligence, Stanley continues to advise clients on issues relating to intellectual property, data protection, content regulation as well as legal tech. Stanley currently serves as the Deputy President of the Copyright Tribunal and sits on the panel of Arbitrators in the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, specializing in the intellectual property disputes. From 1 July 2026, Stanley has been appointed Chairperson of the Data Protection Appeal (DPAP), an independent body that hears appeals against directions or decisions of the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) in relation to data protection provisions in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). From 2026, Stanley has also been appointed to serve as a neutral in the newly formed Patent Mediation and Arbitration Centre under the Unified Patent Court (Europe). Stanley also serves as a Senior Mediator of the Singapore Mediation Centre and as a Specialist Mediator of the Singapore International Mediation Centre. He is an author of many published journal articles and was the first Singapore born lawyer to be conferred a PhD by the University of Cambridge (UK). Stanley was formerly the Chairman of the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS). He was awarded the Public Service Medal (Pingat Bakit Masyarakat) in 2020, and the Public Service Star (Bintang Bakti Masyarakat) in 2024. On 31 August 2022, Stanley was awarded the Singapore Academy of Law Merit Award, which is an award given to individuals who have served in promoting and advancing the objectives of the Singapore Academy of Law. Stanley was appointed Senior Counsel in 2010.

Talvitie first became a Member of Parliament from the electoral district of Oulu in 2015. Since then, she has served as Vice-Chair of the Administration Committee and been a member of various parliamentary committees, such as the Education and Culture Committee, the Environment Committee and the Legal Affairs Committee. Talvitie has been a Member of the Finnish Delegation to the Arctic Parliamentary Conference throughout her years as a Member of Parliament. She has also served as vice-chair of the National Coalition Party's parliamentary group.
Over the course of her political career, she has held the position of vice-chair of the National Coalition Party and chair of the party council of the National Coalition Party. Talvitie has been a member of the Oulu City Council since 2005. She has also chaired the Oulu City Executive, Oulu City Council, Oulu Regional Environmental Committee, Educational Consortium OSAO, and North Ostrobothnia Regional Assembly. Talvitie was also chair of the executive board of the Academic Engineers and Architects in Finland TEK.
Before being elected to Parliament, Talvitie worked in the food industry and as an assistant to several Members of Parliament.
She has a husband and two daughters. Talvitie, who was a girl scout in her youth, enjoys physical exercise, outdoor activities and various cultural pursuits.

Gaétan de Rassenfosse is an Associate Professor of Science, Technology and Innovation Policy at the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland. Trained as an economist, he studies how intellectual property and innovation policies shape the creation, diffusion, and commercialization of knowledge. He holds a Ph.D. in Economics from the Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium.
His research bridges economics, management, and law. His publications have appeared in a wide range of journals, including the Journal of Industrial Economics, Strategic Management Journal, Research Policy, Journal of Law and Economics, Southern California Law Review, among others. His most recent work addresses patent quality, knowledge disclosure, technology commercialization, and the implications of AI-generated inventions for the patent system. He combines economic analysis with large-scale data to examine how intellectual property institutions serve innovators and society.
At EPFL, he teaches intellectual property management and the economics of innovation, introducing students from different disciplines to the economic foundations, legal principles, and strategic uses of IP. He writes The Patentist, a publication that makes economic research on patents accessible to policymakers, practitioners, and a wider audience.
Across his research, teaching, and public engagement, he seeks to bring empirical evidence to debates about how intellectual property can support innovation and the public interest.

people.bio:
AI Domestic Robotics Researcher, PhD candidate in Digital Humanities, University of Vienna, United States of America
Emily Kate Genatowski is an American immersive robotics researcher, historian, and entrepreneur based in Vienna, Austria, who has gained global recognition for her pioneering work in human-AI integration. Her unique research methodology explores the practical, legal, and social friction points that occur when developing technology moves out of laboratory environments and into everyday settings.
Genatowski achieved international prominence through a first-of-its-kind experiment, living full-time in her Vienna residence with "Tova," a Unitree bipedal humanoid robot. By treating her personal home as a robotics lab, she has documented the humanistic realities of sharing physical spaces with humanoid robotics; insights she shares on global stages, including her viral TED talk at TEDAI Vienna. This ongoing immersive ethnographic experiment has transformed her everyday life into inspiration for public discourse on the deployment of domestic humanoids. Emily speaks candidly on the psychological, behavioral, and practical realities of cohabitating with machines.
Before transitioning into immersive robotics research, Genatowski established a diverse career bridging digital humanities and corporate innovation. She holds an undergraduate degree in History from Columbia University and a Master’s degree from Harvard University. She formerly served as the North American coordinator for Google Arts & Culture, where she managed major digital collaborations with world-class institutions, including NASA, the Smithsonian, and the U.S. National Archives.
Currently a PhD candidate in Digital Humanities at the University of Vienna, she designed and taught the university's first academic master's course on AI and Large Language Models in Humanities Research and regularly consults with numerous other Viennese institutions on AI adoption policies. Emily speaks on stages and lecture halls across Europe about the many pain points of human robotic cohabitation and with a mind towards solution oriented thinking, has embarked upon both advocacy and entrepreneurial ventures. In addition to advocating for identity standards for autonomous robotics within the EU, Genatowski is also the founder of PSL, an Austria-based insurtech startup. PSL standardizes hundreds of risk variables across humanoid robotic deployments in five sectors. The confidence-weighted, multivariable risk scores enable specialist underwriters to develop insurance policies for autonomous robotics, helping modern society safely navigate the complex, evolving landscape of physical AI adoption.
people.name: Ms. Emily Kate Genatowski

people.bio:
Cristian León is the Founder and CEO of Drovid Technologies, a Chilean deep-tech company that uses autonomous drones and on-board artificial intelligence to protect forests by detecting risky human activity, the root cause of most wildfires, from the pre-ignition phase.
An electrical engineer by training, Cristian has more than a decade of experience in engineering, technology and entrepreneurship. In 2015 he founded an electrical engineering services company, and he has completed professional programs in technology development management (MIT) and intellectual property (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology).
In 2020 he founded Drovid with a simple question: what if we could stop a fire before it starts? Drovid’s AI operates directly on the drone, detecting risky human activity, smoke and fire, day and night. One of its models, AirWERD, was developed in collaboration with INRIA, which transferred 100% of the rights to Drovid. The technology has been validated in the field with the support of Chile’s national forestry corporation (CONAF) and investigative police (PDI), and has gained commercial validation through a pilot on 2,500 hectares with Forestal Santa Blanca. A second phase is now starting to validate operations, including a latest-generation model that contextualizes human risk, under the Startup Ciencia 2026 grant. A PCT patent application is in progress in dozens of countries.
Cristian represented Chile at the COP28 business mission and, in 2025 and 2026, was nominated by Chile’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs as the country’s representative for the APEC Bio-Circular-Green Award. He is a member of the Sustainable Forest Future Roundtable (Proyecta Chile 2050), where he promotes a prevention-first approach to wildfires. In 2026, Drovid was the winner of the WIPO Global Awards in the ICT startup category.
He leads Drovid’s intellectual property strategy and sustainability vision, with the conviction that protecting nature is not a cost but one of the greatest opportunities of our generation.

Elena Perotti is Executive Director of Media Policy and Public Affairs at WAN-IFRA, the World Association of News Publishers, representing more than 20,000 media brands and 60 national publishers' associations in 120 countries.. For 20 years at WAN-IFRA she has been the person in charge of the relationship with the global community of WAN-IFRA member associations of news media publishers, and main liaison with the organisation's governing bodies. For over a decade she has studied and advocated on the relationship between big tech and publishers on behalf of WAN-IFRA's members, developing an early specialisation in how AI is reshaping the news publishing business. He is a member of the Sustainable Forest Future Roundtable (Proyecta Chile 2050), where he promotes a prevention-first approach to wildfires. In 2026, Drovid was the winner of the WIPO Global Awards in the ICT startup category.
He leads Drovid’s intellectual property strategy and sustainability vision, with the conviction that protecting nature is not a cost but one of the greatest opportunities of our generation.

Her unique research methodology explores the practical, legal, and social friction points that occur when developing technology moves out of laboratory environments and into everyday settings.
Genatowski achieved international prominence through a first-of-its-kind experiment, living full-time in her Vienna residence with "Tova," a Unitree bipedal humanoid robot. Emily speaks candidly on the psychological, behavioral, and practical realities of cohabitating with machines.

An electrical engineer by training, Cristian has more than a decade of experience in engineering, technology and entrepreneurship. In 2015 he founded an electrical engineering services company, and he has completed professional programs in technology development management (MIT) and intellectual property (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology).
In 2020 he founded Drovid with a simple question: what if we could stop a fire before it starts? Drovid’s AI operates directly on the drone, detecting risky human activity, smoke and fire, day and night. One of its models, AirWERD, was developed in collaboration with INRIA, which transferred 100% of the rights to Drovid. The technology has been validated in the field with the support of Chile’s national forestry corporation (CONAF) and investigative police (PDI), and has gained commercial validation through a pilot on 2,500 hectares with Forestal Santa Blanca. A second phase is now starting to validate operations, including a latest-generation model that contextualizes human risk, under the Startup Ciencia 2026 grant. A PCT patent application is in progress in dozens of countries.
Cristian represented Chile at the COP28 business mission and, in 2025 and 2026, was nominated by Chile’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs as the country’s representative for the APEC Bio-Circular-Green Award. He is a member of the Sustainable Forest Future Roundtable (Proyecta Chile 2050), where he promotes a prevention-first approach to wildfires. In 2026, Drovid was the winner of the WIPO Global Awards in the ICT startup category.
He leads Drovid’s intellectual property strategy and sustainability vision, with the conviction that protecting nature is not a cost but one of the greatest opportunities of our generation.
